questions.title: Reticulocyte features
questions.question: Concerning reticulocytes:

options.A: They are smaller than mature erythrocytes
options.B: Appear in peripheral blood not more than 2%
options.E: The first precursor cell in erythropoiesis

explanations.A: Incorrect. Reticulocytes are about the same size as, or slightly larger than, mature erythrocytes, not smaller; they have not yet finished the membrane remodelling that shapes the final biconcave disc.
explanations.B: Correct. Reticulocytes normally make up no more than about 1-2% of circulating erythrocytes in peripheral blood. Brilliant cresyl blue, a supravital stain, is what demonstrates them, precipitating their residual ribosomal RNA into a visible reticular network — the feature the reticulocyte is named for and the reason it is counted as a marker of ongoing erythropoiesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The reticulocyte, like the mature erythrocyte, has already extruded its nucleus at the preceding (normoblast) stage; it does not carry a well-developed nucleus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The reticulocyte's residual ribonucleic material is scattered ribosomal RNA, not organised rough endoplasmic reticulum; that RNA is what the supravital stain precipitates into the visible reticulum.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The proerythroblast, not the reticulocyte, is the first precursor cell of erythropoiesis; the reticulocyte is the last stage before the mature erythrocyte, at the opposite end of the series.

questions.learning_objective: State that reticulocytes normally make up no more than 1-2% of circulating erythrocytes and are demonstrated by brilliant cresyl blue supravital stain.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer letter beside option, p.19

questions.title: What reticulocytes give rise to (past-exam block, دفعة 63)
questions.question: Reticulocytes give rise to:

explanations.A: Correct. The reticulocyte is the last stage of the erythroid series before the mature erythrocyte. Once it loses its residual ribosomal RNA and completes its membrane remodelling, it becomes the mature, biconcave, haemoglobin-filled erythrocyte.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Granulocytes arise from a separate myeloid series (granulopoiesis), not from the reticulocyte, which belongs to the erythroid series.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Platelets are fragments of the megakaryocyte, a separate series (thrombopoiesis) from the erythroid series the reticulocyte belongs to.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Agranulocytes" (lymphocytes and monocytes) are not a maturation product of the reticulocyte; they arise from entirely separate lymphoid and monocytic lines.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Lymphocytes arise from the lymphoid stem cell line, not from the erythroid series the reticulocyte is the terminal step of.

questions.learning_objective: State that the reticulocyte matures directly into the erythrocyte, as the terminal step of the erythroid series.

questions.title: Reticulocyte cytoplasm (past-exam block, دفعة 63)
questions.question: Reticulocyte:

options.A: Represent 10% of erythrocytes in peripheral blood

explanations.A: Incorrect. Reticulocytes normally represent no more than about 1-2% of circulating erythrocytes, not 10%; a figure that high would signal markedly accelerated erythropoiesis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The reticulocyte has not yet accumulated its full haemoglobin content; haemoglobin synthesis continues into this stage rather than already being complete, so its haemoglobin content is lower than the mature erythrocyte's, not higher.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The reticulocyte, like the mature erythrocyte, has already lost the capacity to divide; mitotic capacity is lost earlier in the series, at the polychromatophilic erythroblast stage.
explanations.D: Correct. The reticulocyte's cytoplasm stains basophilic with a supravital stain. That basophilia comes from residual ribosomal RNA left over from the preceding stage. Brilliant cresyl blue precipitates that RNA into the visible reticular network the cell is named for.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The reticulocyte has no nucleus; nuclear extrusion happens at the normoblast stage that precedes it.

questions.learning_objective: State that the reticulocyte's cytoplasm is basophilic because of residual ribosomal RNA, and that it is anucleate and non-dividing.
